<table class="mcards"><tr><th></th><th>Lottery (randomised trial)</th><th>Regression discontinuity</th><th>Difference-in-differences</th><th>Matching</th></tr><tr><th class="rl">What it needs</th><td>Assign who gets the programme by chance, before it starts.</td><td>A score and cut-off that decided who took part, and enough units near the cut-off.</td><td>Outcome measured before and after, for participants and a comparison group on a similar path.</td><td>Recorded characteristics that explain who took part, and similar non-participants.</td></tr><tr><th class="rl">What rules it out</th><td>Programme already running, must cover everyone, or the groups cannot be kept apart.</td><td>No score or rule, a cut-off that was not followed, or scores that could be gamed.</td><td>No comparison group, no way to measure before, or groups already on different paths.</td><td>Take-up driven by something unrecorded, such as motivation, or no similar non-participants.</td></tr><tr><th class="rl">Can still be planned if</th><td>Rollout is phased or places are limited, so a draw can decide who goes first.</td><td>Eligibility is not set yet, so a score and cut-off can decide who joins.</td><td>Earlier data or a cut-off are missing: plan a baseline and follow-up for both groups.</td><td>Collect the key characteristics for both groups; combine with the before and after data if they exist.</td></tr></table><p class="mcards-note">Several methods can be possible at once. Each also needs enough data and a large enough sample, so planning early keeps more options open.</p>
